Short forms used in this section. The number after the colon is the line, at leanVM's pin
\code{a386121f}; a bare \code{:N} is a line of the file last named.

\enquote{Deferred} means: the check is a claim entering the pool, enforced by the opening. The
last column says what the verifier accepts without the check, although it is outside the
relation. The step numbers refer to \cref{tab:gen-table-pub-transcript-table,tab:gen-table-pub-transcript-pub}.

  & with messages of unbounded degree the per-round error $3/|\E|$ becomes $D/|\E|$; at
  $D ≥ |\E|−1$ a prover sends a polynomial agreeing with the true round polynomial everywhere
  but at 0 and fixes the sum there \\

  with $v_{\mathrm{cond}} = 1, b = 0$ (branch not taken on a nonzero condition) \\
\textbf{Target derived from the leaf claims} (no transmitted target)
  & \code{05:151-155}; \code{08:76} & \code{cpu/mod.rs:728-735} & \code{py:1393}

\paragraph{The top limb, source by source.} All three pool the claim with value 0 and send
nothing for it. The recursion guest does the same (\code{aggregate.py:1688-1689}:
\code{claim_pool[GEN ** claim_idx] = 0}). A public word with a nonzero top limb: excluded by the
specification's definition; rejected by the Rust verifier before any message is read (the Rust
prover only \code{debug_assert!}s it, \code{cpu/mod.rs:552-555}); not expressible in the Python,
nor in leanISA, whose \lean{PublicInput} is four lanes of $\K$
(\file{LeanerVM/Semantics/Memory.lean:101-110}, leanerVM \code{b435631}), so the Rust's rejection
has no counterpart to model.

\subsubsection{Around the two phases}\label{sec:gen-table-pub-checks-around}

The stream is fully consumed (\code{cpu/mod.rs:769}, \code{vs.finish()}; \code{py:1414}):
trailing scalars reject. Every 192-bit pattern is an element of $\E$, so stream scalars have no
canonicity check (\code{py:104-106} requires 24 bytes).

(The citation check made this precise: it holds of the scalars of these two phases, but the
stream is not check-free in general. The root's two scalars are decoded by
\code{scalars_to_hash}, which rejects a non-canonical half (\code{transcript.rs:95-99},
\code{Error::NonCanonicalEncoding}), and the announced sizes must have zero high limbs
(\code{cpu/mod.rs:133-135}; \code{py:1373}).)
